source.title: RNN Training along Locally Optimal Trajectories via Frank-Wolfe Algorithm
source.authors: Yun Yue; Ming Li; Venkatesh Saligrama; Z. Zhang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper; no cutoff or garbling that prevents reading was apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own RNN training experiments, but uses a different model family and reports training loss or test accuracy rather than the training classification error named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper tests a Frank-Wolfe RNN optimizer against SGD and TBPTT. It reports plotted training losses on sequence tasks, but does not test any listed version's specific claim about CIFAR classification error, spurious minima, depth and shortcuts, initialization, stability-limit learning rates, or batch normalization speed.
record.test_reason: The study compares RNN optimizers on sequence tasks. Its results do not test any listed version: it varies neither initialization, width, depth, residual shortcuts nor learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold. Its BN compatibility comparison reports final test accuracy and total runtime, which cannot establish faster accuracy gains or higher learning-rate tolerance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: their optimizer improves training stability, outperforms their SGD baselines, improves TBPTT, and achieves comparable deep-RNN test accuracy with fewer gradient updates and less training time. They also conclude that it is robust to noisy inputs. These are the authors' claims; the paper inconsistently names some baselines SGD and Adam.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a two-loop Frank-Wolfe RNN optimizer and compares it with SGD and TBPTT; it does not apply the claim's listed recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparisons vary optimizer, inner iteration K, dataset, and architecture; the text says increasing K can reduce the gradient updates needed for convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed Frank-Wolfe optimizer improves or stabilizes vanilla RNN training losses on sequence tasks; on IndRNN it achieves comparable test accuracy with less reported training time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Frank-Wolfe RNN optimizer can improve training efficiency and robustness on sequence tasks relative to the tested baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: Table III reports Ours+BN accuracy/runtime of 94.37%/0.36 hours on HAR-2 and 89.38%/0.41 hours on Noisy-HAR-2, but gives no BN learning curves or learning-rate tolerance comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed RNN optimizer is compatible with batch normalization on HAR sequence tasks.

record.problems: Training-loss values are presented in figures without numeric extraction in the text. The reported test accuracies do not establish training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained. Figures 3–6 and Tables II–III report other optimizer, dataset, architecture, and test-accuracy conditions; these do not measure the training classification error named by the versions. The adding task is a regression task and is outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted or random labels and recipe-dependent failures.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, special plain-network initialization and Fixup.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and initialization-dependent trainable depth.
Loss, curvature and divergence dynamics relative to the initial or evolving stability threshold.
BN effects on accuracy gain over training and learning-rate tolerance; normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All six rows describe the study's own optimizer performance rather than tests of V1–V6. Their cannot_determine states concern the listed claims, not whether the text reports optimizer improvements. Initialization references and statements that IndRNN uses BN are background or recipe descriptions, not controlled tests.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100, convolutional networks, random or corrupted labels, and training classification error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, depth-related training error, and the cited special initialization or normalization-free residual recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and trainable depth in plain networks.
Learning rates above a stability threshold, loss and curvature dynamics, sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including the Fixup comparison.
